data.text:
Some masked protesters hurled objects and burned tires before a police barricade at Ayala Bridge in Manila on Sunday afternoon. 

In a report by GMA Integrated News' Jonathan Andal on Sunday afternoon, violence erupted between police and some protesters who were trying to reach Mendiola which is near Malacañang Palace. 

Trouble started when unidentified, young men lit several tires on fire in front a shipping container that authorities were using as an obstacle. The report said bottle, paint and rocks were thrown at the cops who were forced to use their riot shields to protect themselves from the flying debris.

Despite the provocation and thick acrid smoke, the cops maintained their formation and did not pursue the rioters.

data.text:
My Take on the "Laban sa Katiwalian" Protests Today

Seeing all these crowds in Manila and across the PH today—Luneta packed, Mendiola turning into a battlefield with water cannons—it's heartbreaking, but let's call it what it is: a scripted chaos. We're all fed up with corruption, sure. That flood control scandal? Billions siphoned off while our streets drown every typhoon season. But who's really pulling the strings here?

First off, the kids. So many young faces out there, chanting and holding signs. Adorable? Sure. But this screams communist playbook 101. The NPA sympathizers and their urban fronts know the drill: drag minors into the front lines because cops hesitate to touch them. Jail time? Persecution? Almost zero risk. It's child endangerment dressed as "youth empowerment." Remember the 2017 Marawi siege or those "peace rallies" that turned violent? Same tactic—use the innocent as human shields to shield the guilty. If you love those kids, keep them in school, not in tear gas clouds.

And don't get me started on the DDS crew—Duterte's die-hards suddenly reborn as anti-graft crusaders? Hypocrisy level: expert. These are the same folks who cheered PRRD's iron-fist era, turning a blind eye to every pork barrel ghost and ghost projects under his watch. 

Newsflash: those flood control anomalies? Unearthed from contracts signed and padded *during* Duterte's tenure. 2016-2022, anyone? Billions funneled to cronies while the poor got promises and puddles. Now they're out there waving red fists (irony much?) against Marcos Jr., acting like they just discovered corruption exists. Selective amnesia much? If DDS cared, they'd audit their hero's 6 years first.

Look, corruption rots us all—past and present admins included. But this protest? It's not about justice; it's a power grab. Reds exploiting rage, trolls amplifying division, and opportunists recycling old grudges. Real change? Vote smarter, demand audits from ALL sides, and protect our kids from being pawns. Wake up, Pinoy. Or we'll all stay underwater—literally and figuratively.

#Philippines #LabanSaKatiwalian #CorruptionExposed #NoToChildPawns

VICE GANDA TO MARCOS: ‘IPAKULONG ANG MGA MAGNANAKAW!’ 🔥

Vice Ganda on Sunday, Sept. 21, lashed out at President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., daring him before tens of thousands at the #TrillionPesoMarch in Quezon City to prove his legacy by jailing corrupt officials.

“Nakatingin kami sa’yo, Pangulong Bongbong Marcos — hindi dahil idol ka namin, kundi dahil sinusuwelduhan ka namin at inaasahan namin na tutuparin mo ang inuutos naming mga employer mo.”

Vice delivered the challenge onstage at the People Power Monument, joined by Gabbi Garcia, Iza Calzado, Catriona Gray, and Nicole Cordoves.

The massive protest, coinciding with the 53rd anniversary of Martial Law, saw interfaith groups, youth, workers and families braving rains and filling portions of EDSA in to denounce the multibillion-peso flood-control scandal.

data.text:
Gaya-Gaya: The Toxic Filipino Habit That's Sabotaging Real Change

Fellow Pinoys, let's talk about our favorite bad habit: "gaya-gaya". You know, that knee-jerk urge to copy everything "trendy" without thinking twice? Right now, while the world watches other countries erupt over genuine, fresh corruption scandals, we're out here aping the chants and placards like it's the latest TikTok challenge. Cool? Nah, it's clueless—and it's costing us.

Case in point: Today's **Trillion Peso March** against the flood control graft mess. Billions siphoned off on pork-barrel projects that leave us drowning every typhoon season. Fair? Absolutely, rage away! But hold up—who uncovered this rot? **Bongbong Marcos Jr.** himself kicked off the independent probe just weeks ago, vowing to jail the thieves no matter who they are. This isn't some ancient Marcos Sr. relic; these shady deals festered under **Duterte's watch** from 2016-2022, with funds funneled to cronies while infrastructure crumbled. And yet, what do we hear echoing from EDSA? "Marcos resign!" 

WTF, talaga? We're not fighting the real villains; we're just LARPing as revolutionaries because it *feels* edgy. This gaya-gaya vibe turns legit outrage into a circus—diverting heat from the Dutertes and their allies who actually greenlit the looting. Want proof it's copycat energy? Organizers admit the Sept. 21 timing nods to anti-dictatorship history, but the anti-Marcos resign calls? Straight out of the opposition playbook, amplified by social media echo chambers.

Time to level up, fam. Channel that fire into demanding accountability *across admins*—Duterte holdovers included. No more blind mimicry; let's build our own damn movement. Or we'll keep flooding... literally and figuratively.

#LabanSaKatiwalian #PHPolitics

My Take on the "Laban sa Katiwalian" Protests Today

Seeing all these crowds in Manila and across the PH today—Luneta packed, Mendiola turning into a battlefield with water cannons—it's heartbreaking, but let's call it what it is: a scripted chaos. We're all fed up with corruption, sure. That flood control scandal? Billions siphoned off while our streets drown every typhoon season. But who's really pulling the strings here?

First off, the kids. So many young faces out there, chanting and holding signs. Adorable? Sure. But this screams communist playbook 101. The NPA sympathizers and their urban fronts know the drill: drag minors into the front lines because cops hesitate to touch them. Jail time? Persecution? Almost zero risk. It's child endangerment dressed as "youth empowerment." Remember the 2017 Marawi siege or those "peace rallies" that turned violent? Same tactic—use the innocent as human shields to shield the guilty. If you love those kids, keep them in school, not in tear gas clouds.

And don't get me started on the DDS crew—Duterte's die-hards suddenly reborn as anti-graft crusaders? Hypocrisy level: expert. These are the same folks who cheered PRRD's iron-fist era, turning a blind eye to every pork barrel ghost and ghost projects under his watch. 

Newsflash: those flood control anomalies? Unearthed from contracts signed and padded *during* Duterte's tenure. 2016-2022, anyone? Billions funneled to cronies while the poor got promises and puddles. Now they're out there waving red fists (irony much?) against Marcos Jr., acting like they just discovered corruption exists. Selective amnesia much? If DDS cared, they'd audit their hero's 6 years first.

Look, corruption rots us all—past and present admins included. But this protest? It's not about justice; it's a power grab. Reds exploiting rage, trolls amplifying division, and opportunists recycling old grudges. Real change? Vote smarter, demand audits from ALL sides, and protect our kids from being pawns. Wake up, Pinoy. Or we'll all stay underwater—literally and figuratively.

#Philippines #LabanSaKatiwalian #CorruptionExposed #NoToChildPawns
